title: Feasibility of an app-supported care concept for geriatric patients after a proximal femur fracture
summary:
PROGRES(S) aims to support the continuity of care from the inpatient rehabilitation clinic to the home environment that the independence of those affected in everyday life can be improved in the long term. In addition, general mobility, strength, endurance and quality of life should be increased and the risk of falls and pain reduced. With this in mind, the PROGRES(S) care concept was developed on the basis of scientific recommendations and a previous qualitative study and with the involvement of patients, physiotherapists and physicians. 
The intervention group uses the PROGRES(S) care concept, which includes therapy and training elements. PROGRES(S) is offered by physiotherapists and supported by an app and starts during regular care in the inpatient rehabilitation clinic and is continued by the participants at home. 
Assessments lasting 60 to 90 minutes are carried out on admission to the study (t0), on discharge from the inpatient rehabilitation clinic (t1), after 12 (t2) and 24 weeks (t3) in order to evaluate the feasibility of PROGRES(S) and to assess the preliminary effects of the intervention compared to the control group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Surgery after femur fracture S72.0, S72.1 , S72.2 ICD-10. 
- Possession of a digital device (smartphone, tablet, laptop or computer)
- Ability to operate the device independently 
- Access to internet at home
- Release into the home environment 
- Signed declaration of consent
- DEMMI 44, Tinetti 18
- Ability to speak and write German
Exclusion criteria:
- People whose fracture has been caused by malignancies
- People who have contraindications (loss of consciousness and cardiovascular disease) for physical activity without medical supervision. If there is any uncertainty regarding suitability for physical training, a medical assessment will be requested. 
- Presence of the following secondary diagnoses: 
- Serious psychological illness: e.g. moderate and severe depressive episode, generalized anxiety disorder, schizophrenia or similar 
- Unstable health condition: e.g. requiring dialysis, chemotherapy at the time of recruitment, red flags for serious illness (nocturnal pain, severe muscle cramps, involuntary weight loss, unexplained symptoms) or similar
- Moderately severe cognitive impairment (Mini Mental State Status <19)
